answer: A sponsor carries 52% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. Because the lotus liability is recorded in the garden ledger at admission, the haven audit makes public the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must therefore place its own capital behind every alias it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 14 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
